title: Foreign Trade Policy, FDI & FPI
desc: Trade policy, SEZs, FDI/FPI and capital convertibility

basic.q: Which government body is primarily responsible for implementing and monitoring India's Foreign Trade Policy?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
basic.e: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, implements and administers India's Foreign Trade Policy.

basic.q: A key departure of the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023 from earlier Exim Policies is that it:
o: Has no terminal date and is dynamic, updated as needed
Is administered by the Ministry of Finance
Applies only to Special Economic Zones
basic.e: Unlike earlier five-year Exim Policies, FTP 2023 has no terminal date, allowing continuous, need-based revisions instead of periodic overhauls.

basic.q: In which year was the Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank) established?
basic.e: EXIM Bank was established in 1982 under the Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981.

basic.q: The Export-Import Bank of India was set up under which legislation?
basic.e: EXIM Bank was constituted under the Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981, and commenced operations in 1982.

basic.q: EXIM Bank of India is best described as:
o: A wholly government-owned apex export finance institution
A joint venture between RBI and SBI
A subsidiary of the World Bank
basic.e: EXIM Bank is a wholly government-owned apex financial institution set up to finance, facilitate and promote India's foreign trade.

basic.q: The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act was enacted in:
basic.e: The SEZ Act, 2005 provided the legal framework for setting up Special Economic Zones in India.

basic.q: The SEZ Rules, which operationalised the SEZ Act, came into effect in:
basic.e: The SEZ Rules, 2006 came into force to operationalise the provisions of the SEZ Act, 2005.

basic.q: Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ), established in 1965, was located at:
basic.e: Kandla in Gujarat became Asia's first Export Processing Zone in 1965; it was later converted into a Special Economic Zone.

basic.q: For the purpose of trade operations, duties and tariffs, a Special Economic Zone is treated as:
o: An integral part of the domestic tariff area
basic.e: SEZs are deemed to be foreign territory for the purposes of trade operations, duties and tariffs, distinguishing them from the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA).

basic.q: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is characterised by:
o: Investment made to acquire a lasting interest and management control in an enterprise
Loans given by foreign governments only
basic.e: FDI reflects the objective of an investor to obtain a lasting interest and effective management control (conventionally 10% or more equity) in an enterprise in another economy.

basic.q: Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) refers to:
o: Investment in stocks and bonds without seeking control or management influence
Direct acquisition of a manufacturing plant abroad
basic.e: FPI involves investment in financial assets like equities and bonds purely for returns, without any intention of control, making it more volatile ('hot money').

basic.q: Foreign Portfolio Investors in India are regulated by:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
basic.e: SEBI regulates FPIs in India under the SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations.

basic.q: The SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, which merged categories like FII, sub-accounts and QFI, were notified in:
basic.e: The SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 consolidated and replaced the earlier FII, sub-account and Qualified Foreign Investor (QFI) categories into a unified FPI framework.

basic.q: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB), which earlier processed government-route FDI approvals, was abolished in:
basic.e: The FIPB was abolished in May 2017, with its approval functions transferred to the concerned administrative ministries/departments, facilitated by DPIIT.

basic.q: Which body now facilitates processing of government-route FDI proposals after the abolition of FIPB?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
basic.e: DPIIT (under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry) now facilitates government-route FDI proposals, which are approved by the concerned administrative ministry/department.

basic.q: Under the 'automatic route' of FDI, a foreign investor:
o: Requires prior approval of the RBI or the government
Only needs to make post-facto filings, without prior approval
Must route funds only through EXIM Bank
basic.e: Under the automatic route, no prior approval from the government or RBI is needed; the investor is only required to make post-investment filings/reporting.

basic.q: India's current account became fully convertible under IMF Article VIII in:
basic.e: India accepted the obligations of IMF Article VIII and made its current account fully convertible in 1994.

basic.q: In the context of SEZ units, 'NFE' refers to:
basic.e: SEZ units are required to be positive Net Foreign Exchange (NFE) earners, i.e., cumulative foreign exchange earnings must exceed cumulative foreign exchange outflow over a specified period.

intermediate.q: The Tarapore Committee of 1997 was constituted to examine:
o: A roadmap towards full Capital Account Convertibility
Merger of FII and FDI categories
intermediate.e: The first Tarapore Committee (1997) examined the feasibility and roadmap for full Capital Account Convertibility in India.

intermediate.q: A second committee under S.S. Tarapore revisited the issue of Capital Account Convertibility in:
intermediate.e: A second Tarapore Committee (2006) was set up to review progress and suggest a further roadmap towards fuller capital account convertibility.

intermediate.q: Under the 'government route' of FDI, investment proposals require:
o: Prior approval of the concerned administrative ministry/department
Approval only from a foreign government
Approval from the World Trade Organization
intermediate.e: Under the government route, the proposal must be approved by the concerned administrative ministry or department, with DPIIT facilitating the process.

intermediate.q: The Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme primarily allows:
o: Duty-free import of capital goods for producing quality export goods, subject to export obligation
Interest-free loans to foreign portfolio investors
Exemption of SEZ units from the NFE requirement
intermediate.e: The EPCG Scheme permits import of capital goods at zero/concessional duty for producing export goods, subject to fulfilling a specified export obligation.

intermediate.q: The Advance Authorisation Scheme under the Foreign Trade Policy allows:
o: Duty-free import of inputs physically incorporated in export products
intermediate.e: The Advance Authorisation Scheme permits duty-free import of inputs that are physically incorporated (after making normal allowance for wastage) in a product meant for export.

intermediate.q: 'Deemed exports' under the Foreign Trade Policy refer to:
o: Transactions in which goods do not leave the country but payment is received in foreign exchange or Indian rupees
Only exports to SEZs by sea route
Exports made exclusively by EXIM Bank
intermediate.e: Deemed exports are transactions where goods supplied do not leave India, but are treated as exports since payment is received in Indian rupees or free foreign exchange, e.g., supplies to EOUs/SEZs.

intermediate.q: The Board of Trade functions primarily as:
o: An advisory body providing periodic inputs on foreign trade policy formulation
A judicial tribunal for trade disputes
A wing of the World Bank
A regulator of foreign portfolio investors
intermediate.e: The Board of Trade is an advisory body that advises the government on policy measures for increasing exports and reviewing the foreign trade policy.

intermediate.q: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) is primarily concerned with:
o: Investigating anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard trade remedy measures
Approving FDI proposals under the government route
intermediate.e: DGTR is the agency responsible for administering trade remedy measures such as anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties and safeguard measures.

intermediate.q: FDI is prohibited in which of the following sectors?
o: Lottery business, including government/private lottery and gambling and betting
intermediate.e: FDI is completely prohibited in sectors such as lottery business, gambling and betting, chit funds, atomic energy, and real estate business (with limited exceptions).

intermediate.q: India's acceptance of IMF Article VIII obligations relates specifically to:
o: Full convertibility of the capital account
Full convertibility of the current account
A ban on foreign portfolio investment
intermediate.e: IMF Article VIII obligations relate to avoiding restrictions on current account transactions; India accepted these obligations in 1994.

intermediate.q: The concept of 'sectoral caps' in India's FDI policy refers to:
o: The maximum percentage of foreign equity permitted in a particular sector
The minimum lock-in period for FPI investment
The ceiling on the number of SEZs permitted per state
The upper limit on EXIM Bank's annual lending
intermediate.e: Sectoral caps denote the maximum level of foreign equity/investment permitted in a given sector under India's FDI policy; caps vary across sectors.

intermediate.q: A sector where FDI is permitted 'up to a certain limit under the automatic route and beyond that under the government route' illustrates that:
o: Sectoral caps can have route-based sub-limits combining both entry routes
Automatic and government routes are always mutually exclusive for any sector
All sectors follow only the automatic route
Government route always implies a total prohibition
intermediate.e: Some sectors permit FDI up to a specified limit via the automatic route, with any investment beyond that threshold requiring government route approval, showing the two routes can coexist for a single sector.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. FDI is generally considered more stable than FPI. 2. FPI involves acquiring management control over an enterprise. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct: FDI is considered more stable long-term capital. Statement 2 is incorrect: FPI does not involve management control; that is a feature of FDI.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding Special Economic Zones: 1. Kandla was Asia's first Export Processing Zone, established in 1965. 2. Units in SEZs are required to be positive Net Foreign Exchange (NFE) earners. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: Kandla (1965) was Asia's first EPZ, later converted to an SEZ, and SEZ units must meet the NFE positivity requirement.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) was abolished in 2017. 2. After its abolition, all FDI proposals now require approval of the concerned administrative ministry. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct (FIPB abolished in May 2017). Statement 2 is incorrect: only government-route proposals need ministry approval; automatic-route investments need no prior approval.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's current account has been fully convertible since 1994. 2. India's capital account is fully convertible. 3. The Tarapore Committee examined the roadmap for capital account convertibility. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is incorrect since India's capital account is only partially convertible, not fully convertible.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 merged the erstwhile FII, sub-account and QFI categories. 2. FPI investment is regarded as relatively volatile compared to FDI. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the 2019 SEBI FPI Regulations unified earlier categories, and FPI flows are commonly termed 'hot money' due to their volatility.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Advance Authorisation Scheme allows duty-free import of inputs used in export production. 2. The EPCG Scheme allows duty-free import of capital goods for export production. 3. Deemed exports require goods to physically leave Indian territory. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 correctly describe the Advance Authorisation and EPCG schemes. Statement 3 is incorrect: in deemed exports, goods do not leave India.

advanced.q: The shift from periodic five-year Exim Policies to the FTP 2023 framework primarily reflects:
o: A move towards continuous, dynamic policymaking rather than fixed-term policy cycles
Complete withdrawal of the government from trade policy
Transfer of trade policy powers to the WTO
advanced.e: FTP 2023 marks a shift from fixed five-year Exim Policies to a dynamic, continuously updated policy framework without a terminal date.

advanced.q: Regarding FDI in chit funds, which statement best reflects the policy position?
o: FDI in chit funds is completely and unconditionally prohibited for all investors
FDI in the chit fund sector is prohibited, though investment by NRIs on a non-repatriation basis is permitted
Chit funds are fully open to 100% FDI under the automatic route
Chit funds require RBI's prior clearance under the government route only
advanced.e: FDI is prohibited in the chit fund business in general, though investment by NRIs on a non-repatriation basis is permitted, unlike a blanket prohibition.

advanced.q: Regarding FDI in 'real estate business', which of the following is an accepted exception under India's FDI policy?
o: Development of townships, housing, built-up infrastructure and construction-development projects
Trading in land parcels for speculative resale
Real estate brokerage services for individual plots
Financing of unregistered real estate agents
advanced.e: While FDI in 'real estate business' per se is prohibited, development of townships, housing and construction-development projects is excluded from this prohibition and permitted.

advanced.q: Trading in Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) under India's FDI policy is:
o: Permitted freely under the automatic route
Permitted only up to a 26% cap
advanced.e: Trading in Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) is among the activities/sectors where FDI is prohibited.

advanced.q: Which of the following sectors is on India's list of activities where FDI is prohibited?
advanced.e: FDI is prohibited in sectors such as Atomic Energy and Nidhi companies, along with lottery, gambling, chit funds, real estate business, and TDR trading.

advanced.q: Which of the following trade remedy measures fall under the mandate of the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR)?
o: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties and safeguard measures
Only tariff-rate quotas on agricultural imports
advanced.e: DGTR administers all three major trade remedy instruments: anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, and safeguard measures, consolidating functions earlier spread across separate directorates.

advanced.q: In India's Balance of Payments, which of the following would be classified under the capital account (capital and financial account)?
o: Foreign Direct Investment and Foreign Portfolio Investment inflows
Remittances from Indian workers abroad (current transfers)
advanced.e: FDI and FPI inflows are recorded under the capital/financial account of the Balance of Payments, whereas trade in goods, services and remittances fall under the current account.

advanced.q: Prior to May 2017, government-route FDI proposals were approved by the:
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
Securities and Exchange Board of India
Reserve Bank of India's Capital Account Division
advanced.e: Before its abolition in May 2017, the FIPB was the single-window body that processed and recommended approval of government-route FDI proposals; this function later shifted to concerned ministries, facilitated by DPIIT.

advanced.q: An exporter importing machinery duty-free under the EPCG Scheme is subsequently required to:
o: Fulfil a specified export obligation within a prescribed period
Convert the machinery into an SEZ asset
Surrender the machinery to DGFT after one year
advanced.e: Under EPCG, duty-free/concessional import of capital goods is conditional upon fulfilling a specified export obligation within a prescribed time frame, failing which duties plus interest become payable.

advanced.q: The conventional equity threshold used by the IMF/OECD to distinguish FDI from FPI is investment of:
o: Around 10 percent or more of equity/voting power
A fixed absolute amount regardless of equity share
advanced.e: Per IMF/OECD convention, an equity stake of around 10% or more, indicating an intent to exert management influence, distinguishes FDI from portfolio investment (FPI).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. FDI in lottery business is prohibited under India's FDI policy. 2. FDI in atomic energy is permitted up to 100% under the automatic route. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct: lottery business is a prohibited sector. Statement 2 is incorrect: atomic energy is itself among the sectors where FDI is prohibited.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. SEZ units are permitted duty-free import of goods for authorised operations. 2. SEZs are treated as part of the Domestic Tariff Area for customs purposes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct: SEZ units get duty-free imports for authorised operations. Statement 2 is incorrect: SEZs are treated as foreign territory, not part of the Domestic Tariff Area, for trade and duty purposes.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The first Tarapore Committee submitted its report in 1997. 2. A second Tarapore Committee examined capital account convertibility again in 2006. 3. India's capital account has since become fully convertible on the recommendations of these committees. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct regarding the two Tarapore Committees. Statement 3 is incorrect: India's capital account remains only partially convertible; full convertibility has not been implemented.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the automatic route, an investor must obtain RBI approval before bringing in FDI. 2. Under the government route, DPIIT itself grants final approval to all FDI proposals. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are incorrect: the automatic route requires no prior RBI/government approval (only post-facto filing), and under the government route, approval is granted by the concerned administrative ministry/department, with DPIIT only facilitating the process.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. FDI is generally recorded as relatively stable, long-term capital in the Balance of Payments. 2. FPI is often referred to as 'hot money' due to its volatility. 3. FPI investment necessarily confers management control over the invested enterprise. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 correctly describe FDI and FPI characteristics. Statement 3 is incorrect: FPI, by definition, does not confer management control, that being a defining feature of FDI.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Kandla was converted from an Export Processing Zone into a Special Economic Zone. 2. The SEZ Act, 2005 was operationalised through the SEZ Rules notified in 2006. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: Kandla, originally an EPZ (1965), was later converted into an SEZ, and the SEZ Act, 2005 was operationalised via the SEZ Rules, 2006.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Trading in Transferable Development Rights is a prohibited activity for FDI. 2. Manufacturing of cigarettes and tobacco products is a prohibited sector for FDI. 3. Development of townships and housing projects is entirely barred from receiving FDI. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: development of townships and housing is an accepted exception, not barred, even though 'real estate business' generally is prohibited.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's current account convertibility under IMF Article VIII was achieved in 1994. 2. Full capital account convertibility in India was also achieved in the same year, 1994. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: India's capital account remains only partially convertible even today; only the current account achieved full convertibility in 1994.

title: Poverty and Unemployment
desc: Poverty line committees, unemployment types, MGNREGA and MPI

basic.q: Which committee introduced India's first official poverty line methodology based on calorie intake norms?
basic.e: The Alagh Committee (1979) devised India's first official poverty line methodology based on calorie norms.

basic.q: As per the Alagh Committee methodology, what was the calorie intake norm prescribed for rural areas?
basic.e: The Alagh Committee prescribed 2400 kcal per capita per day for rural areas and 2100 kcal for urban areas.

basic.q: As per the Alagh Committee methodology, what was the calorie intake norm prescribed for urban areas?
basic.e: The Alagh Committee fixed 2100 kcal per capita per day as the urban calorie norm, lower than the rural norm of 2400 kcal.

basic.q: In which year did the Lakdawala Committee submit its report on poverty estimation?
basic.e: The Lakdawala Committee submitted its report in 1993, introducing state-specific poverty lines.

basic.q: The Lakdawala Committee recommended using the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) to update the poverty line for which segment?
basic.e: The Lakdawala Committee used CPI-IW for urban areas and CPI-AL (Agricultural Labour) for rural areas to update poverty lines.

basic.q: Who chaired the committee that submitted its report on poverty estimation in 2009 under the Planning Commission?
basic.e: The 2009 poverty estimation committee was chaired by Suresh Tendulkar, hence known as the Tendulkar Committee.

basic.q: The Tendulkar Committee moved away from a poverty line based purely on which criterion?
basic.e: The Tendulkar Committee shifted away from a pure calorie-intake norm to a broader consumption basket including health and education expenditure.

basic.q: In which year was the Rangarajan Committee on poverty estimation constituted?
basic.e: The Rangarajan Committee was constituted in 2012 to review the Tendulkar methodology, and it submitted its report in 2014.

basic.q: Who chaired the committee that submitted its poverty estimation report in 2014?
basic.e: The 2014 poverty report was submitted by the committee chaired by C. Rangarajan.

basic.q: In which year was the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) enacted?
basic.e: NREGA was enacted in 2005 and later renamed MGNREGA in 2009.

basic.q: MGNREGA was known by which name prior to its 2009 renaming?
basic.e: MGNREGA was originally called NREGA before being renamed after Mahatma Gandhi in 2009.

basic.q: MGNREGA provides a legal guarantee of how many days of wage employment per rural household in a financial year?
basic.e: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment per year to rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.

basic.q: MGNREGA mandates a minimum participation share for women of at least:
basic.e: MGNREGA mandates that at least one-third of the beneficiaries/participants must be women.

basic.q: MGNREGA is implemented under which central ministry?
basic.e: MGNREGA is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

basic.q: The global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) was first launched in which year?
basic.e: The global MPI was launched in 2010 by UNDP and OPHI, replacing the earlier Human Poverty Index.

basic.q: The global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) was jointly developed by UNDP and which institution?
o: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)
basic.e: The global MPI was developed jointly by UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).

basic.q: India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index is released by which institution?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
basic.e: India's National MPI is released by NITI Aayog, with its first edition in 2021, using NFHS data.

basic.q: Which type of unemployment is typically found in Indian agriculture, where more workers are engaged than actually needed and the marginal productivity of extra workers is close to zero?
basic.e: Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed than required, so removing some workers does not reduce output, common in Indian agriculture.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the Tendulkar Committee's methodology from that of the Lakdawala Committee?
o: Tendulkar used only rural poverty lines
Tendulkar moved to a broader consumption basket including health and education instead of pure calorie norms
Tendulkar abolished state-specific poverty lines entirely
Tendulkar used only CPI-AL for both rural and urban areas
intermediate.e: The Tendulkar Committee shifted from calorie-based norms to a broader consumption basket that included health and education expenditure, unlike the Lakdawala approach.

intermediate.q: What does 'MRP' stand for in the context of the Tendulkar Committee's poverty estimation methodology?
intermediate.e: The Tendulkar Committee used the Mixed Reference Period (MRP) for estimating consumption expenditure.

intermediate.q: Frictional unemployment is best described as:
o: Unemployment caused by an economic recession
Short-term unemployment arising when people are between jobs or searching for better jobs
Unemployment due to a mismatch of skills with job requirements
Unemployment confined to a particular agricultural season
intermediate.e: Frictional unemployment is transitional and short-term, arising when workers are searching for or switching jobs.

intermediate.q: Structural unemployment primarily arises due to:
o: A mismatch between the skills of the workforce and the requirements of available jobs
Workers voluntarily searching for better pay
intermediate.e: Structural unemployment results from a mismatch between workers' skills and the demands of a changing economic structure.

intermediate.q: Which of the following sectors is most associated with seasonal unemployment in India?
intermediate.e: Seasonal unemployment is common in agriculture, where workers remain unemployed during off-seasons.

intermediate.q: Cyclical unemployment is caused primarily by:
o: Fluctuations of the business cycle leading to demand-deficient conditions
intermediate.e: Cyclical unemployment arises from downturns in the business cycle, where deficient aggregate demand reduces employment.

intermediate.q: The term 'educated unemployment' refers to:
o: Unemployment among literate and educated youth
intermediate.e: Educated unemployment denotes joblessness among educated/literate youth, a distinct concern in India's labour market.

intermediate.q: Under MGNREGA, an unemployment allowance becomes payable if work is not provided within how many days of application?
intermediate.e: MGNREGA provides for an unemployment allowance if work is not provided within 15 days of the application.

intermediate.q: Which two organisations jointly assess and publish the global Multidimensional Poverty Index?
intermediate.e: The global MPI is jointly published by UNDP and the OPHI at Oxford University.

intermediate.q: The National Rural Livelihood Mission is also popularly known as:
intermediate.e: The National Rural Livelihood Mission is popularly known as Aajeevika.

intermediate.q: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana was:
o: An earlier rural employment generation scheme
A methodology for calculating the Multidimensional Poverty Index
intermediate.e: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana was an earlier rural employment generation scheme, prior to schemes like MGNREGA.

intermediate.q: The 'head-count ratio' as a poverty measure refers to:
o: Average income of the poorest decile
Proportion of the population living below the poverty line
Total number of BPL ration cards issued
Difference between rural and urban poverty lines
intermediate.e: The head-count ratio is the proportion (or percentage) of the population whose consumption/income falls below the poverty line.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Lakdawala Committee: 1. It introduced state-specific poverty lines. 2. It recommended a uniform poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Lakdawala Committee introduced state-specific poverty lines (statement 1 correct); a uniform poverty line basket for rural and urban areas was recommended later by the Tendulkar Committee, not Lakdawala (statement 2 incorrect).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Tendulkar Committee: 1. It used the Mixed Reference Period for consumption estimation. 2. It retained a pure calorie-intake norm as the sole basis of the poverty line. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Tendulkar Committee used the Mixed Reference Period (statement 1 correct) but moved away from a pure calorie-based norm to a broader consumption basket (statement 2 incorrect).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Rangarajan Committee: 1. It was constituted in 2012. 2. It estimated lower poverty ratios than the Tendulkar Committee. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Rangarajan Committee was constituted in 2012 (statement 1 correct) and submitted its report in 2014, but it estimated higher, not lower, poverty ratios than the Tendulkar Committee (statement 2 incorrect).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about types of unemployment: 1. Disguised unemployment is prevalent in Indian agriculture. 2. Frictional unemployment is caused primarily by downturns in the business cycle. 3. Structural unemployment arises from a mismatch between workforce skills and job requirements. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is incorrect since business-cycle downturns cause cyclical unemployment, not frictional unemployment.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about MGNREGA: 1. It was enacted in 2005, originally as NREGA. 2. It guarantees 100 days of employment specifically to urban households. 3. It mandates at least one-third participation by women. Which of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is incorrect because MGNREGA's guarantee applies to rural households, not urban ones.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The global MPI uses three dimensions—health, education, and standard of living. 2. India's National MPI uses NSSO consumption expenditure survey data as its primary data source. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The global MPI indeed covers health, education, and standard of living (statement 1 correct); India's National MPI uses NFHS data, not the NSSO consumption survey (statement 2 incorrect).

advanced.q: Which committee's poverty line methodology was based on normative levels of adequate nourishment along with non-food essential expenditures such as clothing, rent, conveyance, education, and health?
advanced.e: The Rangarajan Committee (2014) proposed a methodology based on normative nourishment levels plus essential non-food expenditures like clothing, rent, conveyance, education, and health.

advanced.q: After the Rangarajan Committee submitted its report in 2014, what has been the status of official poverty line adoption by the Government of India?
o: The Rangarajan methodology was formally adopted for BPL classification
No poverty line methodology has been formally adopted for official BPL purposes since Rangarajan
The Tendulkar methodology was reintroduced and formally adopted permanently
A new committee replaced Rangarajan's report in 2016
advanced.e: The government has not formally adopted any poverty line methodology for official BPL classification purposes since the Rangarajan Committee's 2014 report.

advanced.q: Unlike the Alagh Committee, the Tendulkar Committee based its poverty line basket primarily on:
o: A broader consumption expenditure basket including health and education, not calories alone
Only urban calorie norms applied nationally
advanced.e: The Tendulkar Committee broadened the poverty line basket beyond calories to include consumption on health and education.

advanced.q: Which committee first introduced state-specific (disaggregated) poverty lines in India's official poverty estimation?
advanced.e: The Lakdawala Committee (1993) was the first to disaggregate poverty lines at the state level.

advanced.q: What is the correct chronological order of India's poverty estimation committees?
advanced.e: The correct chronological sequence is Alagh (1979) to Lakdawala (1993) to Tendulkar (2009) to Rangarajan (2014).

advanced.q: A software professional who has voluntarily left a job and is spending a few weeks searching for a better-paying position best exemplifies which type of unemployment?
advanced.e: This scenario of short-term job search between employments is a classic case of frictional unemployment.

advanced.q: On a farm where a task requiring only 3 workers is performed by 5 workers, with the additional 2 workers contributing near-zero marginal output, this situation is termed:
advanced.e: This is a textbook case of disguised unemployment, common in Indian agriculture, where excess workers add negligible output.

advanced.q: Which type of unemployment is expected to rise sharply during an economic recession marked by falling aggregate demand?
advanced.e: Cyclical unemployment is directly linked to the business cycle and rises during recessions due to demand deficiency.

advanced.q: How does India's National MPI released by NITI Aayog differ from the global MPI framework in terms of data source?
o: It uses the Census of India exclusively
It uses National Family Health Survey (NFHS) data adapted with India-specific indicators
It uses only World Bank poverty estimates
advanced.e: India's National MPI, released by NITI Aayog, adapts the global framework using NFHS data with India-specific indicators.

advanced.q: The Human Poverty Index (HPI), which was replaced by the Multidimensional Poverty Index in 2010, was earlier published by:
advanced.e: The Human Poverty Index, published by UNDP, was replaced by the global MPI (developed jointly with OPHI) in 2010.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Alagh Committee's poverty line was based solely on calorie intake norms. 2. The Lakdawala Committee retained the calorie-anchored poverty lines but updated them over time using CPI-IW and CPI-AL with state-specific disaggregation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: Alagh used pure calorie norms, while Lakdawala retained the calorie-based lines but updated them using CPI-IW/CPI-AL and introduced state-level disaggregation.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about the Tendulkar Committee: 1. It recommended a uniform poverty line basket (PLB) for both rural and urban areas. 2. It completely discarded any reference to a consumption basket and relied only on health and education expenditure. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: The Tendulkar Committee recommended a uniform poverty line basket for rural and urban areas (statement 1 correct), but it broadened rather than discarded the consumption basket, retaining food along with health and education expenditure (statement 2 incorrect).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about the Rangarajan Committee: 1. It was constituted in 2012 and submitted its report in 2014. 2. It concluded that the Tendulkar Committee had overestimated poverty in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct; however, the Rangarajan Committee estimated higher poverty ratios than Tendulkar, implying Tendulkar had underestimated, not overestimated, poverty (statement 2 incorrect).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding poverty estimation committees: 1. The Alagh Committee (1979) was the first to set official calorie-based poverty norms. 2. The Lakdawala Committee (1993) introduced the use of the Mixed Reference Period. 3. The Tendulkar Committee (2009) recommended a uniform poverty line basket for rural and urban areas. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is incorrect since the Mixed Reference Period was introduced by the Tendulkar Committee, not Lakdawala.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about MGNREGA: 1. It provides a legal guarantee of employment only to households classified as Below Poverty Line (BPL). 2. It is a demand-driven scheme. 3. An unemployment allowance is payable if work is not provided within 15 days of application. Which of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; statement 1 is incorrect because MGNREGA guarantees employment to any rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work, not restricted to BPL households.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about types of unemployment: 1. Seasonal unemployment is essentially the same concept as disguised unemployment. 2. Structural unemployment can arise from changes in the economic structure, such as automation displacing certain job skills. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 correctly describes structural unemployment; statement 1 is incorrect as seasonal unemployment (joblessness during off-seasons) is conceptually distinct from disguised unemployment (excess workers with near-zero marginal productivity).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements on the Multidimensional Poverty Index: 1. The global MPI uses three dimensions—health, education, and standard of living. 2. The global MPI was developed jointly by UNDP and OPHI. 3. India's National MPI's first edition used Census 2011 data as its primary source. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is incorrect since India's National MPI, released by NITI Aayog, is based on National Family Health Survey (NFHS) data, not the Census.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Rangarajan Committee proposed a separate methodology from the Tendulkar Committee based on normative nourishment levels and non-food essentials. 2. The Rangarajan Committee's estimated poverty ratio was lower than that estimated by the Tendulkar Committee. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is incorrect because the Rangarajan Committee estimated a higher, not lower, poverty ratio compared to the Tendulkar Committee.

title: Human Development and Social Sector
desc: HDI, HDR, related indices and SDGs

basic.q: Which economist is credited with pioneering the concept of the Human Development Index (HDI), working alongside Indian economist Amartya Sen?
basic.e: Mahbub ul Haq, a Pakistani economist, pioneered the HDI concept along with Amartya Sen in the late 1980s, drawing on Sen's capability approach.

basic.q: The first Human Development Report (HDR) was published by UNDP in which year?
basic.e: The first Human Development Report was published by the UNDP in 1990.

basic.q: The Human Development Report is published annually by which organisation?
basic.e: The HDR is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), usually with a special thematic focus each year.

basic.q: In the Human Development Index, the dimension of 'a long and healthy life' is measured using which indicator?
basic.e: The health dimension of HDI is captured through life expectancy at birth.

basic.q: Which indicator is used to measure the 'decent standard of living' dimension of the HDI?
o: Per capita income at market exchange rates
Gross National Income (GNI) per capita at Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
basic.e: The standard-of-living dimension is measured by Gross National Income (GNI) per capita at PPP, which allows cross-country comparability.

basic.q: The 'knowledge' dimension of the HDI is constructed using which two indicators?
o: Literacy rate and school enrolment ratio
Expected years of schooling and mean years of schooling
Public expenditure on education and literacy rate
basic.e: The education dimension combines expected years of schooling (for children entering school) and mean years of schooling (for adults aged 25 and above).

basic.q: Since which Human Development Report has the HDI been calculated using the geometric mean of the three dimensional indices?
basic.e: From the 2010 Human Development Report onward, HDI has been computed as the geometric mean of the health, education and income indices, replacing the earlier arithmetic mean.

basic.q: Based on HDI value, countries are classified into how many categories of human development?
basic.e: Countries are grouped into four categories: very high, high, medium, and low human development.

basic.q: What does IHDI, an index reported alongside HDI in the Human Development Report, stand for?
basic.e: IHDI stands for Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index, which discounts the HDI value for inequality in the distribution of each dimension across the population.

basic.q: The Gender Development Index (GDI) is defined as:
o: The average of male and female literacy rates
The ratio of female HDI to male HDI
A composite index of women's political representation
The gender gap in labour force participation rate
basic.e: The GDI is the ratio of the female HDI to the male HDI, capturing gender gaps in the same three basic dimensions used in HDI.

basic.q: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) measures inequality between men and women across which three dimensions?
o: Reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation
basic.e: The GII captures gender-based inequality in reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation.

basic.q: For the Gender Inequality Index (GII), which of the following is true?
o: A higher GII value indicates lower gender inequality
A lower GII value indicates lower gender inequality
GII has no defined direction of interpretation
A GII value of 1 indicates perfect equality
basic.e: Unlike HDI, for GII a lower value indicates lower inequality, i.e., better gender equality outcomes.

basic.q: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), published alongside the HDR, covers deprivations in which three dimensions?
basic.e: The MPI captures overlapping deprivations in health, education, and living standards at the household level.

basic.q: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) featured in the Human Development Report was jointly developed by UNDP with which institution?
o: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)
basic.e: The MPI was jointly developed by UNDP with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).

basic.q: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by UN Member States in September 2015 at which forum?
basic.e: The SDGs were adopted by all UN Member States at the UN General Assembly in September 2015.

basic.q: How many goals and targets do the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) comprise?
basic.e: The SDGs comprise 17 Goals and 169 targets, forming the core of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

basic.q: The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), which preceded the SDGs, were in effect during which period and comprised how many goals?
basic.e: The MDGs ran from 2000 to 2015 and comprised 8 goals, largely focused on developing countries.

basic.q: In India, which institution is the nodal agency for coordinating implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
basic.e: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for SDG coordination in India and publishes the SDG India Index to track progress of states and UTs.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is a key difference between the SDGs and the MDGs?
o: MDGs had more goals than SDGs
SDGs apply universally to both developed and developing countries, while MDGs were largely focused on developing countries
MDGs were adopted by UNDP while SDGs were adopted by the UN General Assembly
SDGs have fewer targets than MDGs
intermediate.e: A defining shift from MDGs to SDGs is universality: SDGs apply to all countries, whereas MDGs were largely framed around developing-country concerns.

intermediate.q: Why did the Human Development Report shift from an arithmetic mean to a geometric mean in calculating HDI from 2010 onward?
o: To simplify the calculation for smaller economies
To penalize imbalance/inequality between the three dimensions, since poor performance in one cannot be fully offset by good performance in another
To align HDI calculation with GDP growth accounting
To remove the education dimension from the index
intermediate.e: The geometric mean penalizes imbalance across dimensions -- a low score in one dimension cannot be fully compensated by a high score in another, unlike the arithmetic mean used earlier.

intermediate.q: How does the Gender Development Index (GDI) differ from the Gender Inequality Index (GII)?
o: GDI and GII measure identical concepts and are interchangeable
GDI compares female and male HDI values across the same three HDI dimensions, while GII is a separate composite index covering reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation
GII is published by the World Bank while GDI is published by UNDP
GDI is calculated only for developed countries
intermediate.e: GDI is the ratio of female-to-male HDI across the standard HDI dimensions, whereas GII is a distinct composite index built around reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation.

intermediate.q: A major criticism of the Human Development Index (HDI) is that it:
o: Does not include an education dimension at all
Does not directly capture inequality, poverty, human security, or empowerment
Cannot be calculated for developing countries
intermediate.e: HDI is criticized for being a summary measure that does not directly capture inequality, poverty, human security or empowerment -- separate indices like IHDI, MPI and GII were developed to address such gaps.

intermediate.q: What is the key purpose of publishing the Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI) alongside the standard HDI?
o: To rank countries solely on income levels
To show the loss in human development due to unequal distribution of health, education, and income within a country
To replace GNI per capita with GDP per capita
intermediate.e: The IHDI adjusts the HDI downward to reflect the loss in potential human development caused by inequality in distribution of the three dimensions across the population.

intermediate.q: Amartya Sen's 'capability approach', which influenced the conceptualisation of the HDI, primarily emphasizes:
o: Maximizing GNP growth as the sole indicator of development
Expanding people's real freedoms and capabilities to lead the kind of life they value, rather than focusing only on income
Measuring development purely through consumption expenditure
Prioritizing industrial output over agricultural output
intermediate.e: The capability approach shifts the focus of development from mere income/GNP growth to expanding people's freedoms and capabilities to achieve valuable functionings.

intermediate.q: What is the primary function of the SDG India Index, published by NITI Aayog?
o: To rank Indian states/UTs based on GDP growth
To measure and monitor the progress of Indian states and Union Territories on the Sustainable Development Goals
To assess India's global HDI rank
To calculate India's Gender Inequality Index
intermediate.e: The SDG India Index, published by NITI Aayog, tracks the progress of states and Union Territories on SDG indicators.

intermediate.q: Who served as the lead author associated with the first Human Development Report in 1990?
intermediate.e: Mahbub ul Haq was the driving force and lead author behind the first HDR in 1990, though the underlying capability framework drew on Amartya Sen's work.

intermediate.q: 'Expected years of schooling' and 'mean years of schooling', both used in HDI, differ in that:
o: Both measure the same thing for adults only
Expected years of schooling projects schooling for a child entering the school system, while mean years of schooling reflects the actual average schooling completed by adults aged 25 and above
Mean years of schooling is a forward-looking projection while expected years of schooling is historical
Expected years of schooling applies only to girls
intermediate.e: Expected years of schooling is a forward-looking projection for children currently entering school, while mean years of schooling reflects the actual average years completed by adults aged 25+.

intermediate.q: Which statement best distinguishes the philosophical basis of human development thinking from earlier welfare economics approaches?
o: Human development thinking equates development with rising per-capita GNP alone
Human development thinking, drawing on the capability approach, views development as expanding people's real freedoms/capabilities, going beyond income-centric measures
Welfare economics rejects the use of any economic indicators
There is no conceptual difference between the two approaches
intermediate.e: Traditional welfare economics often equated development with rising income/GNP; the capability approach reframed development as expanding real freedoms, influencing the HDI's multidimensional design.

intermediate.q: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) differs from conventional income-based poverty measures in that MPI:
o: Relies solely on income thresholds like the poverty line
Captures overlapping deprivations across health, education, and living standards experienced simultaneously by a household
Is calculated only for urban populations
intermediate.e: Unlike income-based poverty lines, MPI identifies the poor based on overlapping deprivations across health, education, and living standards simultaneously.

intermediate.q: Which of the following about the Human Development Report's special annual theme is correct?
o: Every HDR since 1990 has carried the same fixed theme
Each year's HDR usually carries a distinct special theme relevant to contemporary human development concerns
HDR themes are decided by the World Bank
HDR has never had thematic focuses
intermediate.e: Each year's Human Development Report typically carries a distinct special theme reflecting contemporary development concerns, alongside the routine HDI rankings.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Human Development Index incorporates income inequality directly as one of its three dimensions. 2. The health dimension of HDI is measured using life expectancy at birth. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect -- HDI's three dimensions are health, education and income levels, not inequality directly (that is captured separately by IHDI). Statement 2 is correct -- life expectancy at birth measures the health dimension.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Millennium Development Goals comprised 17 goals. 2. The Sustainable Development Goals were adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2015. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect -- the MDGs had 8 goals, not 17 (17 is the number of SDGs). Statement 2 is correct -- the SDGs were adopted at the UN General Assembly in 2015.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding indices published in the Human Development Report: 1. The Gender Inequality Index (GII) covers reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation. 2. The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) was developed jointly with OPHI. 3. A higher GII value indicates lower gender inequality. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect -- for GII, a lower value indicates lower inequality, not a higher one.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. HDI classifies countries into four categories of human development. 2. The 'decent standard of living' dimension of HDI is measured using GDP per capita at market exchange rates. 3. HDI has been calculated using the geometric mean of dimensional indices since the 2010 Human Development Report. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect -- the standard-of-living dimension uses GNI per capita at PPP, not GDP per capita at market exchange rates.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI) can never be higher than the standard HDI value for a country with any inequality. 2. The IHDI and HDI would be identical only in a hypothetical case of perfect equality. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct -- the IHDI is always less than or equal to HDI, with equality holding only when there is no inequality in the distribution of dimensions.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding NITI Aayog's role in India's SDG framework: 1. NITI Aayog is the nodal agency coordinating SDG implementation in India. 2. NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index to track progress of states and UTs. 3. NITI Aayog also publishes the global Human Development Report. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect -- the global Human Development Report is published by UNDP, not NITI Aayog.

advanced.q: Why does the HDI use GNI per capita at Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) rather than nominal GDP per capita at market exchange rates for its income dimension?
o: PPP adjusts for differences in price levels/cost of living across countries, giving a more comparable measure of real standard of living
Nominal GDP double-counts remittances received by a country
PPP-based figures are always lower than market exchange rate figures for every country
GNI at PPP excludes agricultural income from the calculation
advanced.e: GNI per capita at PPP adjusts for differing price levels and cost of living across countries, enabling a more meaningful cross-country comparison of real purchasing power/standard of living than nominal GDP at market exchange rates.

advanced.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the 'capability approach' from a narrow 'human capital' approach to development?
o: The capability approach treats people as the ends of development (expanding freedoms to achieve valued functionings), while human capital approaches often treat people primarily as a means to economic growth/production
The capability approach focuses only on physical capital accumulation
The human capital approach is broader and includes political freedoms while the capability approach does not
There is no meaningful conceptual distinction between the two
advanced.e: The capability approach views human beings as the ends of development, valuing expanded freedoms, whereas a narrower human capital lens often treats people as inputs (means) to raise productivity and growth.

advanced.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three basic dimensions used to construct the HDI?
advanced.e: HDI's three dimensions are health, education and standard of living; inequality is not a direct HDI dimension -- it is addressed separately through the IHDI.

advanced.q: Which document forms the core framework within which the SDGs were adopted?
o: The Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
advanced.e: The SDGs form the core of the '2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development', adopted alongside the goals in September 2015.

advanced.q: In terms of interpretation direction, which pairing is correct?
o: For both HDI and GII, a higher value always indicates a better outcome
For HDI, a higher value indicates better human development, whereas for GII, a lower value indicates lower (better) gender inequality
For HDI, a lower value indicates better human development, whereas for GII, a higher value indicates better gender equality
Neither HDI nor GII has a defined direction of interpretation
advanced.e: HDI is a positively-oriented index (higher is better), while GII is inversely oriented -- a lower GII value signals lower/better gender inequality outcomes.

advanced.q: How does the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) complement the information provided by the HDI?
o: MPI duplicates HDI exactly at the household level
MPI captures the intensity and overlap of deprivations experienced by individual households across health, education and living standards, information the aggregate/national-level HDI does not reveal
MPI replaces HDI as UNDP's primary human development measure
MPI is calculated using only income data, unlike HDI
advanced.e: While HDI is a national aggregate, MPI identifies overlapping, simultaneous deprivations experienced by individual households, offering granularity that HDI does not capture.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements about the historical evolution of the HDI methodology is correct?
o: HDI has used the geometric mean since its inception in 1990
HDI initially used an arithmetic mean of the three dimensional indices, and switched to a geometric mean from the 2010 Human Development Report onward
HDI has never changed its method of aggregating dimensional indices
HDI switched from geometric mean to arithmetic mean in 2010
advanced.e: HDI originally aggregated its three indices using an arithmetic mean; this changed to a geometric mean starting with the 2010 HDR.

advanced.q: The universality of the SDGs, as opposed to the MDGs, implies which of the following?
o: SDGs apply only to least-developed countries
SDGs set targets and goals applicable to developed and developing countries alike, unlike MDGs which were framed largely with developing countries in mind
SDGs exclude environmental goals, unlike MDGs
SDGs are legally binding treaties, unlike MDGs
advanced.e: The SDGs mark a shift to universality -- applicable to all UN member states -- whereas the MDGs largely targeted developing-country outcomes such as poverty and child mortality.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly relates GDI to HDI?
o: GDI is a completely independent index unrelated to HDI's dimensions
GDI uses the same three basic dimensions as HDI but is calculated separately for females and males, then expressed as a ratio
GDI is calculated only using the income dimension of HDI
GDI is a synonym for GII and both are computed identically
advanced.e: GDI disaggregates the same three HDI dimensions by sex, computing separate female and male HDI values, and expresses GDI as their ratio.

advanced.q: Why is the HDI often described as a 'summary' measure of human development rather than a comprehensive one?
o: Because it is calculated only once every ten years

Because it condenses multidimensional aspects of development into a single composite number using only three dimensions, thereby omitting other important aspects like inequality, security and empowerment
Because it only applies to G20 countries
Because it excludes the education dimension entirely
advanced.e: HDI is a summary/composite measure based on just three dimensions; it deliberately simplifies development into a single number, leaving out inequality, human security, empowerment, etc., which other indices seek to address.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) featured in the HDR is based purely on monetary income thresholds. 2. The MPI is published jointly with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect -- MPI is based on overlapping non-monetary deprivations (health, education, living standards), not just income. Statement 2 is correct -- MPI is a joint product of UNDP and OPHI.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The geometric mean used in HDI since 2010 allows very poor performance in one dimension to be fully compensated by very high performance in another dimension. 2. The geometric mean reduces the degree of substitutability between the dimensional indices compared to the arithmetic mean. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect -- that describes the effect of the earlier arithmetic mean, not the geometric mean. Statement 2 is correct -- the geometric mean reduces substitutability and penalizes imbalance across dimensions.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The HDI was first introduced in the 1990 Human Development Report. 2. Since 2010, HDI has been the arithmetic mean of the health, education and income indices. 3. The concept of HDI was influenced by Amartya Sen's capability approach. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect -- since 2010 HDI uses the geometric mean, not the arithmetic mean.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Gender Development Index (GDI) is expressed as the ratio of female HDI to male HDI. 2. The Gender Inequality Index (GII) is expressed as the ratio of female HDI to male HDI. 3. The GII ranges in value from 0 to 1, with 0 indicating equality between men and women. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect -- that description applies to GDI, not GII; GII is a separate composite index of reproductive health, empowerment and labour market participation, not a simple HDI ratio.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The MDGs were in effect from 2000 to 2015 and comprised 8 goals. 2. The SDGs, comprising 17 goals, were adopted to succeed the MDGs. 3. The SDGs are legally binding treaties ratified by national legislatures. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect -- the SDGs are a set of globally agreed goals/targets under the 2030 Agenda, not a legally binding treaty requiring ratification.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. HDI classifies countries into 'very high', 'high', 'medium' and 'low' human development categories. 2. The Human Development Report has been published biennially (once every two years) since 1990. 3. The MPI assesses deprivations at the household level across health, education and living standards. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect -- the HDR has been published annually, not biennially, since 1990 (with only rare exceptions).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Mahbub ul Haq was an Indian economist who pioneered the HDI along with Pakistani economist Amartya Sen. 2. The capability approach underlying HDI's conceptualisation shifted the development discourse away from a narrow focus on GNP growth. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 reverses the nationalities -- Mahbub ul Haq was Pakistani and Amartya Sen is Indian, not the other way around. Statement 2 is correct -- the capability approach reoriented development thinking beyond GNP growth.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding the SDGs in the Indian context: 1. NITI Aayog coordinates SDG implementation and monitoring in India. 2. The SDG India Index measures progress of Indian states and Union Territories on SDG-related indicators. 3. India's SDG framework replaced the need for any human development indices at the sub-national level. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect and overstated -- the SDG framework does not eliminate the relevance of other human development indices at sub-national levels.

title: Inclusive Growth and Financial Inclusion
desc: Inclusive growth, PMJDY, MUDRA, DBT and JAM trinity

basic.q: Which Five Year Plan explicitly adopted 'faster and more inclusive growth' as its central theme?
basic.e: The 11th Five Year Plan (2007-12) was titled 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth', making it the central theme of that plan.

basic.q: The concept of inclusive growth primarily emphasizes which of the following?
o: Broad-based growth that reduces poverty and inequality across sectors and regions
Growth concentrated in urban industrial hubs
Growth measured only through stock market performance
basic.e: Inclusive growth is broad-based across sectors, includes a large share of the labour force, and reduces poverty, inequality and regional disparities, rather than being judged by GDP growth alone.

basic.q: Which RBI committee defined financial inclusion as ensuring access to financial services and timely, adequate credit to vulnerable groups at an affordable cost?
basic.e: The Rangarajan Committee on Financial Inclusion (2008) gave this widely cited definition of financial inclusion.

basic.q: The Nachiket Mor Committee (2013-14) was constituted to examine which subject?
o: Comprehensive financial services for small businesses and low-income households
basic.e: The Nachiket Mor Committee was the 'Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low-Income Households', set up by the RBI in 2013-14.

basic.q: The Nachiket Mor Committee's recommendations led to RBI guidelines in 2014 for licensing of which two new categories of banks?
o: Payments Banks and Small Finance Banks
Regional Rural Banks and Cooperative Banks
basic.e: Following the Nachiket Mor Committee's recommendation for differentiated bank licenses, the RBI issued 2014 guidelines for licensing Payments Banks and Small Finance Banks.

basic.q: On what date was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) launched?
basic.e: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 as the National Mission for Financial Inclusion.

basic.q: PMJDY is officially described as the National Mission for which of the following?
basic.e: PMJDY was launched as the National Mission for Financial Inclusion.

basic.q: Which of the following is a key feature of a PMJDY basic savings bank deposit account?
o: Minimum balance of Rs 5,000 is mandatory
Zero-balance account with a RuPay debit card carrying accident insurance cover
Only available to salaried government employees
basic.e: PMJDY accounts can be opened with zero balance and come with a RuPay debit card that has an inbuilt accident insurance cover.

basic.q: PMJDY entered the Guinness World Records for which achievement?
o: Highest number of bank accounts opened in a single week
basic.e: As part of the financial inclusion campaign, PMJDY set a Guinness World Record for the highest number of bank accounts opened in a single week.

basic.q: What does MUDRA stand for in the context of Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana?
o: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency
Ministry of Urban Development and Rural Assistance
Microfinance Unit for Development and Rural Advancement
Micro Union for Development and Regional Assistance
basic.e: MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency.

basic.q: In which month and year was the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) launched?
basic.e: PMMY was launched in April 2015.

basic.q: Under MUDRA, what is the maximum loan amount covered under the 'Shishu' category?
basic.e: The 'Shishu' category covers loans up to Rs 50,000.

basic.q: Under MUDRA, the 'Tarun' loan category covers loans in which range?
o: Above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh
Above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh
Above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh
basic.e: The 'Tarun' category covers loans above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh, the highest MUDRA slab.

basic.q: What is the maximum loan amount available to a beneficiary under the MUDRA scheme?
basic.e: MUDRA provides collateral-free loans of up to Rs 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.

basic.q: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) was launched in India on which date?
basic.e: DBT was launched on 1 January 2013 to reform government delivery systems.

basic.q: The primary objective of the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) scheme is to:
o: Increase import duties on subsidised goods
Transfer subsidies and benefits directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts to reduce leakages and delays
Replace all bank branches with mobile banking units
Provide collateral-free loans to micro enterprises
basic.e: DBT aims to transfer subsidies/benefits directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts, reducing leakages, delays and duplication in welfare delivery.

basic.q: The 'JAM Trinity' popularized in the Economic Survey 2014-15 refers to which combination?
basic.e: The JAM Trinity stands for Jan Dhan (bank accounts), Aadhaar (unique identity), and Mobile (connectivity).

basic.q: Aadhaar, the unique identity number issued by UIDAI, consists of how many digits?
basic.e: Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identity number issued by the UIDAI.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Inclusive growth is measured solely by the rate of GDP growth. 2. Inclusive growth seeks to reduce rural-urban and regional disparities. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect since inclusive growth is not judged by GDP growth alone; statement 2 is correct as inclusive growth addresses regional and rural-urban disparities.

intermediate.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Rangarajan Committee from the Nachiket Mor Committee?
o: Rangarajan Committee recommended differentiated bank licenses; Nachiket Mor Committee defined financial inclusion
Rangarajan Committee (2008) defined financial inclusion; Nachiket Mor Committee (2013-14) recommended structural reforms including differentiated bank licenses
Both committees were set up in the same year with identical mandates
Neither committee was constituted by the RBI
intermediate.e: The Rangarajan Committee (2008) provided the definition of financial inclusion, while the Nachiket Mor Committee (2013-14) recommended structural reforms such as differentiated bank licenses.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding MUDRA loan categories: 1. 'Shishu' covers loans up to Rs 50,000. 2. 'Kishor' covers loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh. 3. 'Tarun' covers loans above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is incorrect because 'Tarun' covers loans above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh, not Rs 20 lakh.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains why the JAM Trinity is considered central to India's financial inclusion strategy?
o: It combines bank accounts, unique identity, and mobile connectivity to enable direct transfer of benefits and plug leakages
It refers to three separate insurance schemes for the poor
It is a committee formed to review MUDRA loan defaults
It denotes three types of Payments Banks licensed by RBI
intermediate.e: The JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile) enables direct benefit transfer, reduces leakages in subsidy delivery, and furthers financial inclusion.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. PMJDY accounts can be opened with zero balance. 2. PMJDY provides an overdraft facility for eligible account holders. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: PMJDY allows zero-balance accounts and provides an overdraft facility for eligible account holders.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is an accurate distinction between MUDRA loans and PMJDY overdraft facility?
o: MUDRA loans are collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh for non-farm micro enterprises, while PMJDY overdraft is a smaller facility linked to a basic savings account
MUDRA loans require collateral while PMJDY overdraft does not
Both are identical schemes launched on the same date
MUDRA loans are only for agricultural purposes
intermediate.e: MUDRA provides collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh for non-corporate, non-farm micro enterprises, whereas the PMJDY overdraft is a smaller credit facility tied to a basic savings account.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. DBT relies on the JAM trinity architecture. 2. PAHAL is a DBT scheme for LPG subsidy transfer. 3. DBT was launched after the Aadhaar Act, 2016 came into force. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because DBT was launched on 1 January 2013, before the Aadhaar Act, 2016 was enacted.

intermediate.q: Under MUDRA, loans are extended to beneficiaries mainly through which channel?
o: Directly by MUDRA to all end-borrowers
Banks, NBFCs, and MFIs, with MUDRA refinancing/supporting these last-mile financiers
intermediate.e: MUDRA loans are extended by banks, NBFCs, and MFIs, with MUDRA largely refinancing and supporting these last-mile financiers rather than always lending directly.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about UIDAI is correct?
o: UIDAI was set up in 2009 and issues the 12-digit Aadhaar number
UIDAI was established under the Aadhaar Act, 2016 for the first time
UIDAI is a committee under the Ministry of Finance that studies financial inclusion
UIDAI issues RuPay debit cards to PMJDY account holders
intermediate.e: UIDAI was set up in 2009 and is responsible for issuing the 12-digit Aadhaar number; statutory backing came later via the 2016 Act.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act was enacted in 2016. 2. This Act gave statutory backing to Aadhaar. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct; the 2016 Act provided statutory backing to Aadhaar for targeted delivery of subsidies and benefits.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature associated with PMJDY?
o: RuPay debit card with accident insurance cover
Collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh for micro enterprises
Overdraft facility for eligible account holders
intermediate.e: Collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh for micro enterprises are a feature of MUDRA, not PMJDY.

intermediate.q: Which of the following correctly reflects the chronology of these initiatives?
o: DBT (2013) preceded PMJDY (2014), which preceded MUDRA (2015)
MUDRA (2015) preceded PMJDY (2014), which preceded DBT (2013)
PMJDY (2014) preceded DBT (2013), which preceded MUDRA (2015)
All three were launched in the same year
intermediate.e: The correct chronology is DBT (1 January 2013) then PMJDY (28 August 2014) then MUDRA (April 2015).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. PAHAL (DBTL) is used for transferring LPG subsidy directly to beneficiaries. 2. PAHAL once held a Guinness World Record for the largest cash transfer/subsidy benefit programme. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct; PAHAL is a major DBT scheme for LPG subsidy and once held a Guinness World Record for the largest such programme.

intermediate.q: The differentiated banking licenses recommended following the Nachiket Mor Committee report resulted in the creation of which two categories?
o: Rural Banks and Urban Cooperative Banks
Payments Banks and Small Finance Banks
Public Sector Banks and Private Sector Banks
intermediate.e: The Nachiket Mor Committee's recommendations led to RBI's 2014 guidelines creating Payments Banks and Small Finance Banks.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between financial inclusion and inclusive growth?
o: They are unrelated concepts with no overlap
Financial inclusion, by extending affordable credit and financial services to weaker sections, serves as a means towards achieving inclusive growth
Inclusive growth is a subset of financial inclusion
Financial inclusion refers only to GDP growth targets
intermediate.e: Financial inclusion extends access to affordable financial services to weaker sections, thereby supporting the broader goal of inclusive growth.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. MUDRA loans are available only to registered corporate entities. 2. MUDRA loans are collateral-free. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect since MUDRA targets non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises; statement 2 is correct as MUDRA loans are collateral-free.

intermediate.q: Why is the DBT scheme considered dependent on the JAM trinity architecture?
o: Because DBT requires beneficiaries to have a Jan Dhan account, an Aadhaar-linked identity, and a mobile number to receive transfers efficiently
Because DBT was launched by the JAM committee in 2013
Because JAM refers to three types of MUDRA loans
Because DBT only covers mobile phone subsidies
intermediate.e: DBT relies on the JAM trinity — bank accounts, Aadhaar-based identity verification, and mobile connectivity — to transfer benefits directly and reduce leakages.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements correctly compares the objectives of PMJDY and DBT?
o: PMJDY aims to provide universal access to basic banking services, while DBT aims to transfer subsidies directly into existing bank accounts to cut leakages
PMJDY and DBT are identical schemes with the same launch date
DBT provides RuPay cards while PMJDY transfers LPG subsidies
PMJDY was launched to reduce fiscal deficit while DBT promotes banking access
intermediate.e: PMJDY focuses on providing access to basic banking services, while DBT uses such accounts to transfer subsidies directly, reducing leakages and delays.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The 11th Five Year Plan was the first to use GDP growth rate as its sole indicator of success. 2. The 11th Five Year Plan's title reflected a shift towards addressing distributional concerns alongside growth. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as inclusive growth explicitly moved away from judging success by GDP growth alone; statement 2 is correct, reflecting the plan's focus on faster and more inclusive growth.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding the evolution of financial inclusion policy in India: 1. The Rangarajan Committee (2008) preceded the Nachiket Mor Committee (2013-14). 2.
